quotes.why: The exact list the paragraph quotes: Haribhadra's six names, which Chökyi Gyaltsen reproduces word for word.
The tail of the same Haribhadra sentence: the functions, the 'primordially at peace' clause and the closing label, which are what the paragraph's second, third and fourth headings take in turn.
Haribhadra's gloss on the five eyes a few lines earlier, where the divine eye is qualified as 'born of ripening', the counterpart of 'born of formative effort' in this paragraph.
The root lemma: the six superknowledges as the eighth of the ten instructions of the first chapter.
Ārya Vimuktisena states outright the distinction that Haribhadra's qualifier 'born of formative effort' encodes: the five-eyes divine eye is born of ripening, the superknowledge one of dhyāna.
Chökyi Gyaltsen himself, a few pages on, explaining the one qualifier in this paragraph and citing both of Haribhadra's phrases and Vimuktisena for it. Found by direct search.

quotes.text: དེ་གང་ཞིག ཉོན་སྒྲིབ་ཟད་པར་སྤངས་པ་དེ། ཟག་ཟད་ཀྱི་མངོན་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། ཁ་ཅིག མཚན་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཚིག་ཟུར་དུ་སྒྲིབ་གཉིས་སྤངས་པའི་ཐབས་དང་། སྤངས་པའི་སྤངས་པ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པ། ཞེས་སྦྱོར་མི་རིགས་ཏེ། ཉན་ཐོས་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་ཟག་ཟད་ཀྱི་མངོན་ཤེས་ཀྱིས་སྒྲིབ་གཉིས་སྤངས་པའི་སྤངས་པ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་མ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཕྱིར།
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen defining the sixth superknowledge by afflictive obscurations alone and refusing a two-obscurations wording, against the grain of Haribhadra's gloss. Found by direct search.
Gyaltsab Je's gloss on the sixth superknowledge, whose wording is very close to the ཁ་ཅིག definition Chökyi Gyaltsen rejects.
Gyaltsab Je placing the five eyes and six superknowledges in the ten instructions: the causes of independent practice and of the swift completion of the result.
Gyaltsab Je unpacking 'the divine eye born of formative effort' as a subtle physical organ produced by meditation in this life, with the superknowledge a mental consciousness relying on it.
Panchen Sonam Drakpa openly declining to take Gyaltsab Je's account of the divine eye literally: the Drepung Loseling side of the dispute.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's own ruling on the same question: the divine-eye and divine-ear superknowledges are mental, not sense, consciousnesses. Found by direct search.
